name: Shemaiah
overview: Shemaiah was a male Levite known for being sent by King Jehoshaphat to fulfill a specific role as recorded in 2 Chronicles 17:8. His identity as a Levite highlights his connection to the tribe entrusted with priestly duties in Israel. There are no additional notes providing further background on his life or ministry.
namesAndTitles: The name Shemaiah means 'YHWH hears,' reflecting a theologically rich meaning rooted in the Hebrew language. This proper name underscores the biblical theme of God’s attentive presence toward His people. The name is not indicated as being given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Shemaiah as a descendant of Levi, confirming his tribal lineage. Beyond this, there are no recorded family relationships or further genealogical details provided in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Shemaiah’s significance lies in his role as a Levite dispatched by King Jehoshaphat, which implies a trust in his service within the religious or administrative functions of the kingdom. His mention in 2 Chronicles 17:8 situates him within the context of Jehoshaphat’s efforts to strengthen the spiritual life of Judah through the Levites. Through this, Shemaiah exemplifies faithful service in God’s appointed order during a period of religious reform.
